title: Lift a set-valued stalk equivalence to abelian group objects
statement: Let C be a category with objects in Type (u+1) and morphisms in Type u, J a Grothendieck topology, p a Type-u-valued point of J [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and G a topological group. Put w=max(u+1,v), D=Rep.DiscreteContinuousRep Z G [def-exc-discrete-modules-category], U its inclusion into Rep Z G, and V the inclusion of discrete continuous G-actions into all G-actions. Given an equivalence Eset:Sh(J,Type w) ≌ DiscreteContAction(Type w,G) and a natural isomorphism j from its underlying-set functor to the stalk p, there are an equivalence E:Sh(J,AddCommGrpCat w) ≌ D and an additive stalk comparison i. The underlying G-action functor of E is naturally isomorphic to forgetting the abelian sheaf and applying Eset. Moreover, for every abelian sheaf F, g in G, object X, pointed lifts x,x' in p(X), and section z in F(X), if j sends the g-translate of the set-valued germ of z at x to its germ at x', then i sends the g-translate of the abelian germ of z at x to its germ at x'.

proof.text: Transport integer internal modules along the supplied equivalence Eset using [lem-pod-equivalence-induces-module-objects]. Equivalences preserve finite products. Identify internal integer modules in sheaves of sets with abelian-group-valued sheaves, since products and the sheaf condition are computed on underlying sets. Identify internal integer modules in discrete continuous G-sets with integer representations with open stabilizers [def-exc-discrete-modules-category]. These identifications preserve operations and morphisms and give E and the underlying-action natural isomorphism.

proof.text: Naturality of j with respect to the group operations and its cartesian compatibility lift it to an additive stalk comparison i. Let gamma be the canonical underlying-set/additive-stalk comparison from Mathlib GrothendieckTopology.Point.sheafFiberCompIso, and beta the equivariant underlying-action comparison from step 1. Choose i with gamma composed with forget(i) equal to j composed with forget(beta). This equation, equivariance of beta, and compatibility of gamma with maps from sections identify the images of the two additive germs with the set-valued germs in the premise. Apply gamma to the desired equality, use the premise, and use injectivity of gamma. This gives the action implication independently of any field or choice of Galois extensions.
